idiom_name: serializer + mapper writing one LOB column
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep one column for the serialized value and ordinary columns for identity, lookup and versioning. A serializer converts the graph into a single payload that embeds a format version, and a mapper owns the round trip so domain objects stay persistence-ignorant. Choose a language-neutral, non-executable format (JSON, CBOR, protobuf) when anything other than the current process must read the payload, and a general serialization framework when the payload is strictly private to one process and version. Whatever the format, version it inside the payload, treat the stored bytes as untrusted input on read, and decide up front how old payloads will be upgraded or re-serialized.
code_sketch:
row = { id: 1, kind: 'diagram', payload: LOB }     # identity outside, graph inside
payload = serializer.dump(graph, version = 3)      # the version travels with the data
store.put(row.id, payload)
graph = serializer.load(store.get(row.id))         # validate, upgrade older versions
pitfalls: No format version inside the payload: the first class change turns stored rows into unreadable data.
Serializing a whole aggregate that other tables reference by foreign key, which recreates a shadow schema without integrity.
Deserializing stored values with a format that can instantiate arbitrary classes (Java serialization, pickle, Marshal, BinaryFormatter) - a storage bug becomes remote code execution.

Wrong move: when a reporting need appears, keep filtering in application code by deserializing every stored row -> loading thousands of payloads to find a handful becomes a full-table scan plus deserialize storm -> instead promote the handful of fields the database must filter or index into real indexed columns (or a projection table) before shipping, and leave only genuinely opaque data in the payload.

Wrong move: two requests read the same row, each mutate one nested field and write the whole blob back -> the last writer silently wins and the first edit vanishes -> instead guard the row with a Version Number (optimistic lock) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and re-apply or reject on conflict.

Wrong move: let the payload grow unbounded as real data accumulates -> writes start failing at row/blob/packet limits (MySQL max_allowed_packet, PostgreSQL TOAST, SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH) and backups, replication and caches bloat -> instead bound the graph, monitor payload sizes, and move media or bulk history to an object store with only a reference in the row.
